newsitem.title: NEPAL: Japan to fund $453 mln Nepal hydroelectric plant.
newsitem.headline: Japan to fund $453 mln Nepal hydroelectric plant.

text.p: Japan has agreed to fund a $453 million power project in Nepal which when completed in 2001 will be the biggest hydroelectric scheme in the Himalayan kingdom, officials said on Friday.
Japan would provide 8.68 billion rupees ($153 million) for the Kali Gandaki project 180 km (110 miles) west of Kathmandu, Finance Ministry spokesman Mahesh Karki said.
"With this we have completed raising funds for Kali Gandaki," Karki told Reuters.
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has already provided $160 million for the project expected to generate 144 megawatts of electricity.

The state-run Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA), which owns all power plants in the country, would mobilise the remaining funds by increasing electricity rates and cutting operation costs, officials said.
Nepal is among the world's poorest nations, but is counted among the world's richest in terms of hydroelectric potential which totals 83,000 megawatts.
But it has to import power to meet a current shortfall in generation. Only 15 percent of the kingdom's 21 million people are supplied with electricity.
